A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpaCE-10 and provide readable main text, tables, figures and appendices. The retained benchmark, annotation pipeline and experiments can be matched reliably despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original model and human evaluations, basic-versus-compositional QA experiments, and annotation-pipeline ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original evaluations and ablations and adds model results, dataset analyses, unweighted rankings and GPT-5 case outcomes.

M1.justification: v3 Section 3.2 says GPT-4o generates EQ questions from label-derived counts; v4 Section 3.2 and Appendix D.1 specify predefined templates. This is a limited revision to the described generation procedure. The hierarchical pipeline and cross-capability integration otherwise remain.

E1.justification: Both retain the same four source datasets, 811 indoor scenes, eight QA types, and image/point-cloud and single/multiple-answer coverage. The added analyses and examples do not establish new datasets, domains or task scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands from 25 to 46 evaluated models, adding GPT-5, InternVL3/3.5 variants, Gemma3, GLM-4.5V and others while retaining all earlier models. Conversely, v3 Table 6's additional multiple-answer comparators, including GPT4Scene and the closed-source models, disappear; v4 retains the smaller Table 3 comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the human reference from an average of two people to six experts. Appendix G adds unweighted overall scoring alongside the retained weighted ranking. The eight-frame evaluation input is newly disclosed, without evidence that it changed from v3.

E4.justification: v4 adds vocabulary and character-length analyses, capability co-occurrence analysis, an unweighted ranking, and GPT-5 success/failure cases across the existing tasks. The composition ablation in Table 4 and pipeline ablation in v3 Table 7/v4 Table 6 retain their numerical results; the original QA-quality cases are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated model runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The increased human participant count changes the evaluation sample size without adding uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v4 Table 2 adds results including GPT-5 at 53.4% and InternVL3.5-241B-A28B at 55.0%. Retained overall scores change from 35.4% to 35.9% for InternVL2.5-4B and from 37.9% to 38.7% for Qwen2.5-VL-72B. The human reference changes from 85.3% to 91.2% with more participants. Unweighted and case-study results are added, while extended multiple-answer and all-model capability results are removed.

T1.justification: The task-capability mapping and substantive capability definitions remain. Appendix E explains the existing capability score using a standard mean formula and toy example; no new theorem, proof or substantive theoretical development is established.

C1.justification: The benchmark, hierarchical-pipeline, human-performance-gap and counting-bottleneck claims remain. The introduction strengthens the composition claim from questions often involving more than three capabilities to every QA type covering more than five, and broadens the stated evaluation contribution to nearly 50 models.

C2.justification: v4 develops new interpretations concerning capability hierarchy, divergence between overall accuracy and capability scores, counting limitations under scaling, and capability-focused training. It removes v3 Section 5's explicit qualifications about annotation errors and limited applicability beyond small indoor scenes.

D1.justification: v4 adds the eight-frame evaluation input, explicit five-option/two-correct-answer rules, worked QA transformations and capability-score computation details. It removes the scene-selection split instructions and explicit Table 2 weights. The repository link changes from Cuzyoung to VisionXLab, and the direct dataset link is omitted.

R1.justification: The broad MLLM/VQA survey is replaced by a focused spatial-intelligence narrative. Appendix C newly grounds the capability design in Sparkle and other prior work, with additions including SpatialRGPT, MMScan and EgoExoBench. Table 1 replaces the multi-capability criterion with CSI, under which VSI is marked negative rather than its earlier positive multi-capability designation.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, dataset overview and capability-analysis narrative are substantially rewritten. The appendices are reorganized into separate definition, generation, scoring, ablation and case-study sections, and references move before them. Terminology shifts toward single-answer/multiple-answer, although usage remains inconsistent.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a six-panel analysis, Figure 4 is recolored with revised model selection, and Table 2 expands substantially. v4 adds an unweighted-results table and Figures 9–22, removes the extended multiple-answer table and full-model heatmap, and relocates retained examples and interface figures. Figure 2's caption incorrectly describes a correlation panel where capability coverage is displayed.

improvement.justification: v4 broadens model comparisons, corrects retained scores and provides useful construction details and diagnostics. However, it removes explicit split instructions, weight values, scope limitations and supplementary results. New reporting also conflicts internally: GPT-5 scores differ between Table 2 and the prose, while Appendix E describes per-question averaging and Section 4.3 describes per-QA-type averaging. These benefits and losses in transparency and consistency do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
